avoid_supplements.name: Iron supplements
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Iron chelates ciprofloxacin, reducing its bioavailability by up to 90%, compromising antibiotic efficacy
avoid_supplements.action: Separate administration by at least 2-4 hours; take ciprofloxacin 2 hours before or 6 hours after iron

avoid_supplements.name: Zinc supplements
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Zinc forms insoluble complexes with ciprofloxacin, significantly reducing absorption
avoid_supplements.action: Separate administration by at least 2-4 hours; prioritize ciprofloxacin dosing first

avoid_supplements.name: Magnesium supplements
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Magnesium chelates ciprofloxacin and decreases its absorption by 50-90%
avoid_supplements.action: Administer ciprofloxacin 2 hours before or 6 hours after magnesium supplementation

avoid_supplements.name: Calcium supplements
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Calcium forms insoluble complexes with fluoroquinolones, reducing bioavailability significantly
avoid_supplements.action: Separate administration by at least 2-4 hours; take ciprofloxacin before calcium intake

avoid_supplements.name: Aluminum-containing antacids
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Aluminum chelates ciprofloxacin, reducing absorption by up to 90%
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use; separate by at least 2-4 hours, preferably 6 hours

avoid_supplements.name: Tizanidine
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Ciprofloxacin inhibits CYP1A2 metabolism of tizanidine, causing dangerous accumulation and severe hypotension
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use; use alternative fluoroquinolone or muscle relaxant

avoid_supplements.name: Caffeine supplements
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Ciprofloxacin inhibits CYP1A2, reducing caffeine metabolism and increasing risk of CNS stimulation, tremor, and tachycardia
avoid_supplements.action: Reduce caffeine intake during ciprofloxacin therapy; monitor for excessive stimulation

caution_supplements.name: NSAIDs (including supplemental forms)
caution_supplements.mechanism: Combined use may increase risk of tendon rupture and CNS stimulation effects
caution_supplements.action: Use lowest effective dose of NSAID; monitor for tendon pain or CNS symptoms

caution_supplements.name: Probiotics
caution_supplements.mechanism: Ciprofloxacin kills beneficial bacteria; probiotics may partially mitigate antibiotic-associated diarrhea
caution_supplements.action: May consider probiotics 2+ hours apart from ciprofloxacin dosing; no absolute contraindication

caution_supplements.name: Ginseng
caution_supplements.mechanism: Theoretical increase in CNS stimulation when combined with fluoroquinolone-induced effects
caution_supplements.action: Monitor for dizziness, tremor, or insomnia; consider temporary discontinuation if symptoms occur

avoid_foods.name: Dairy products (milk, cheese, yogurt)
avoid_foods.mechanism: Calcium and magnesium in dairy chelate ciprofloxacin, reducing absorption by 30-50%
avoid_foods.action: Avoid dairy products within 2-4 hours of ciprofloxacin; take antibiotic on empty stomach or with non-fortified juice

avoid_foods.name: Fortified juices (orange juice, apple juice)
avoid_foods.mechanism: Fortified with calcium or magnesium salts that chelate ciprofloxacin and reduce bioavailability
avoid_foods.action: Avoid fortified juices; use water or non-fortified beverages with ciprofloxacin

caution_foods.name: Caffeine-containing foods/beverages (coffee, tea, chocolate)
caution_foods.mechanism: Ciprofloxacin inhibits CYP1A2, prolonging caffeine half-life and increasing stimulatory effects
caution_foods.action: Moderate caffeine intake during treatment; monitor for jitteriness, insomnia, or tachycardia

caution_foods.name: High-fiber foods
caution_foods.mechanism: Excessive fiber may slightly reduce ciprofloxacin absorption; minimal clinical impact
caution_foods.action: No strict avoidance needed; ensure adequate hydration and maintain normal fiber intake

monitoring_notes: Ciprofloxacin absorption is critically dependent on proper spacing from divalent/trivalent cations (iron, zinc, magnesium, calcium, aluminum); administer on empty stomach with water only for optimal bioavailability. Monitor for QT prolongation risk, tendinopathy, and CNS effects, particularly in elderly patients or those with concurrent risk factors.
